### Purpose
The stated purpose is to control Q/K gauge symmetry drift in learnable multipliers without shrinking multiplier magnitudes as weight decay does. Paper [16] discusses gauge redundancy in positively homogeneous neural networks and introduces gauge-adapted coordinates to address scale imbalances, which aligns with the goal of controlling gauge symmetry drift. While [16] does not explicitly address Q/K multipliers, the underlying purpose of managing gauge symmetry drift is substantively equivalent.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, GaugeFix-LRM, involves an explicit gauge-fixing projection that balances Q/K scales while preserving the attention function exactly. Paper [16] introduces a soft gauge-fixing functional inspired by field theory to address scale redundancy in neural networks, which is conceptually equivalent to the gauge-fixing projection described here. Additionally, paper [9] discusses gauge fixing for sequence-function relationships, which involves removing gauge freedoms to make model parameters interpretable. Both [16] and [9] employ gauge-fixing primitives, making the mechanism covered.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses GPT-2 124M trained on OpenWebText. Papers [1], [17], and [22] evaluate GPT-2 models on similar datasets, such as OpenWebText or other web-based corpora, using standard pretraining setups. The evaluation design (training a GPT-2 model on a web corpus) is therefore covered.

### Domain
The domain is language model training with attention gauge symmetry and learnable multipliers. Paper [1] explicitly addresses learnable multipliers in language model training, and papers [4] and [16] discuss gauge symmetry in the context of attention mechanisms and neural networks. These papers collectively cover the domain.
